title: Geomagnetic storms predicted for this weekend could bring the northern lights to...
text:
ByMary Whitfill Roeloffs,

Forbes Staff.

The aurora borealis could light up skies into the northern United States Friday and Saturday nights thanks to a geomagnetic storm that will push the Kp index to almost six and extend the visibility of the northern lights slightly below the Canadian border.

The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration predicts a Kp index of 4.6 for Friday night and 5.6 for the early hours of Saturday morning, meaning the aurora may be “quite pleasing” to see in the right places.

NOAA has predicted geomagnetic storms to arrive from Friday to Sunday—–including a G2 class storm in the early hours of Saturday morning—spurred by the arrival of multiple coronal mass ejections, or eruptions of plasma and magnetic fields from the sun's outer atmosphere.

Saturday night may also provide a chance at seeing the northern lights, as NOAA has issued a Kp index of 4.6.

NOAA’s forecast shows a chance of seeing the northern lights in Washington, Idaho, Montana, North Dakota, northern Wyoming, South Dakota, Minnesota, northern Wisconsin and Michigan. Those states have a relatively low chance of catching the lights compared to much of Alaska, where a “high” chance of visibility is forecast for a large portion of the state’s interior (see below). If there is a G2 geomagnetic storm, the viewline could be extended to include Oregon, Nebraska, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, New York, Vermont and New Hampshire.

The best chance of seeing the lights usually comes between between 10 p.m. and 2 a.m. local time, according to NOAA. Hopeful viewers should travel as far north as possible to a high, north-facing vantage point away from light pollution.

Those using an iPhone should use night mode and those with an Android should use the device’s Pro mode. All smartphone photographers should disable flash and shoot in RAW image format. Those using a separate camera could set the aperture or F-stop to four or less and use a focus set to the furthest possible setting. All photographers should use a tripod for stabilizing the image.
